items.text: Thousands of leftwing protesters marched in France after Emmanuel Macron appointed conservative Michel Barnier as prime minister. Demonstrators, led by France Unbowed (LFI), accused Macron of undermining democracy, saying his decision ignored the July election results. France’s parliament is split between three main groups: the leftwing New Popular Front (NFP), Macron’s centrist bloc, and the far-right National Rally (RN). Barnier, from the center-right, faces opposition from leftwing parties, which had proposed their candidate. Barnier has said he may include representatives from the left in his government. The protests signal growing tensions in the country, with many accusing Macron of relying on the far-right for support. Difficult words: undermine (to weaken), signal (to show). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Thousands of protesters in France marched against President Emmanuel Macron’s choice of a conservative prime minister, Michel Barnier. The leftwing group France Unbowed led the protesters and said this decision was unfair and ignored the results of the recent elections. After the elections, no group won a majority in the parliament. The leftwing New Popular Front (NFP) got the most seats, but Macron didn’t choose their candidate for prime minister. Barnier, who used to work as a Brexit negotiator, said he would try to bring all groups together. The protests may continue in the coming weeks. Difficult words: conservative (a person who supports traditional values and ideas), ignore (to not pay attention to someone or something), majority (the greater number). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of people in France protest. President Emmanuel Macron chooses a new prime minister . Macron chooses Michel Barnier. Barnier is a conservative politician. Many people are angry. They think that Macron does not care about the results of the election. In the election, no party wins enough seats to have full control. The leftwing group, NFP, gets the most seats. But Macron does not choose their candidate for prime minister. The protesters say this is not fair. Barnier says that he will try to work with different political groups. Many people think the protests will continue. Difficult words: prime minister (the boss of a government), conservative (someone who likes old ideas), candidate (a person who competes to get a job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On September 9th, Pope Francis visited East Timor, marking the first papal visit to the predominantly Roman Catholic country since its independence from Indonesia. While the capital, Dili, was in a festive mood, controversy emerged over a massive new altar built for the Pope’s visit. The construction cost around 1 million dollars and displaced many residents. Some families were forced to leave their homes and businesses, and they are concerned about their future as they await unclear compensation . The local church claims responsibility for the altar’s construction but distances itself from the evictions , saying it is the government’s decision. East Timor has a strong historical connection to the Catholic Church, as Pope John Paul II visited during the Indonesian occupation in 1989. While the previous papal visit inspired protests for independence, this one has sparked debate over the social and economic cost. Difficult words: papal (relating to a pope or the Roman Catholic Church), compensation (money awarded to someone), eviction (money paid to someone in exchange for something that has been lost or damaged, or for some problem). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On September 9th, Pope Francis visited East Timor. It was the first papal visit since the country became independent from Indonesia. The capital, Dili, was celebrating the Pope’s visit, but there was also some anger. Workers built a new altar for the Pope, which cost about 1 million dollars. But local people had to leave their homes because of the project. Many families are unsure where they will go next, and they are waiting for money promised by the government. The church says it is only responsible for building the altar and that the government decided to move people. East Timor has a special connection to the Catholic Church. Pope John Paul II visited the country in 1989, during Indonesian rule. Difficult words: papal (related to a pope or the Roman Catholic Church), altar (raised place for religious ceremonies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pope Francis visits East Timor on September 9th. This is the first time a Pope visits the country since it becomes free from Indonesia. People in the capital, Dili, are happy. But some people are angry. Workers build a new altar for the Pope. It costs about 1 million dollars. Many families have to leave their homes because of it. These people do not know where they will live next. The church says that they only built the altar. But the government tells people to move. East Timor has a close history with the Catholic Church. In 1989, Pope John Paul II visits the country. At that time, it is still part of Indonesia. Difficult words: Pope (the head of the Roman Catholic Church), altar (a special place for church ceremonies), history (things which happen in the past). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Olympic marathon runner Rebecca Cheptegei has tragically passed away after being attacked by her former boyfriend. The 33-year-old Ugandan athlete, who competed in the Paris Olympics, suffered severe burns after being doused with petrol and set on fire in Kenya. She died four days later due to organ failure caused by burns covering over 70% of her body. The attack occurred when she returned from church with her two daughters. Her ex-boyfriend, who also sustained burns, is being treated in the ICU . Authorities are investigating the incident, raising concerns about the rising violence against female athletes, particularly in Kenya. Cheptegei began competing in 2010, representing Uganda in various competitions. She won a gold medal in a mountain running event in 2022 and lived and trained in Kenya, a region famous for producing top athletes. Her death has shocked the athletic community, who remember her as a friendly and talented person. Difficult words: doused (to be covered with liquid), ICU (intensive care unit in a hospital). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Rebecca Cheptegei, a 33-year-old Ugandan marathon runner, died after her ex-boyfriend attacked her. He poured petrol on her and set her on fire. The attack happened in Kenya after she returned from church with her daughters. Cheptegei was badly burned and died four days later in the hospital due to her injuries. Her ex-boyfriend is also in the hospital with burns. Since 2021, three female athletes died, which raised concerns about the safety of women athletes. Cheptegei started running for Uganda in 2010. She won a gold medal in mountain running in 2022 and competed in the Paris Olympics. People who knew her said she was a kind and friendly person. Difficult words: pour (to make something flow from a container), burned (hurt by heat or fire), concern (a worried or nervous feeling about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rebecca Cheptegei is a runner from Uganda. She is in the Paris Olympics. Her ex-boyfriend attacks her. He pours petrol on her and sets her on fire. This happens after she comes home from church in Kenya. Rebecca is very hurt. She dies four days later. Her ex-boyfriend is also hurt and in the hospital. Rebecca starts running for Uganda in 2010. She also wins a medal in mountain running. People say that she is very kind and friendly. Rebecca is from Uganda but lives and trains in Kenya. She is the third woman athlete who dies in Kenya since 2010. Difficult words: attack (to try to hurt someone), pour (to make something flow from a container), medal (a prize for winning a race or competition). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China has announced it will no longer allow international adoptions. This change aligns with international agreements and only allows the adoption of stepchildren or close relatives. It brings uncertainty for families in the process. Over the past 30 years, at least 150,000 Chinese children were adopted abroad, with the majority of 82,000 going to the US. One expert explained that adoptions have been paused since 2020, partly due to demographic concerns. China now values children more highly and has programs for special needs, reducing the need for international adoptions. Additionally, there is a growing sentiment that Chinese children should remain in their home country due to cultural differences. As China’s middle class has grown and poverty has been reduced, more local families are encouraged to adopt. Social attitudes are changing, and many families are now more open to adoption, especially if having biological children is difficult. Difficult words: demographic (related to population changes), sentiment (an opinion or idea based on a feeling about a situation), biological child (a child who is genetically related to their parents). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

China said it would stop foreign adoptions. This means that families in other countries will not be able to adopt Chinese children. This decision is in line with international rules. In the past 30 years, foreign families adopted over 150,000 Chinese children, most children going to the US. A Chinese expert mentioned that this rule change could be because China’s population is shrinking , and they now have ways to help children in the country. International adoptions paused in 2020. China believes children should stay in China because of cultural differences, and today, the country needs children more than in the past. Also, the Chinese government encourages families to adopt children instead of sending them overseas. People are more open to adopting children if they can’t have their own. Difficult words: in line with (under control), shrink (to become smaller), encourage (to make someone more likely to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China will no longer let families from other countries adopt children from China. Before, many children go to other countries to live with families. Most children go to the US, about 82,000. Now, China says that children should stay in China. In 2020, China stops sending children for adoption to other countries. China’s population is getting smaller. It is not good to send their children away. China thinks that children are very important. Chinese government asks families in China to adopt. Today, people in China are more open to adopting children. One of the reasons is that many people have problems having their own child. Difficult words: adopt (to take in a child as your own), population (all the people in a country), reason (why something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Greece, Lake Mornos, a crucial water source for nearly half of the population, has significantly decreased in size due to extreme weather conditions. After a winter with little snow and a summer of intense heatwaves and drought, the lake has shrunk to its lowest level in decades. As the water recedes , the remains of the village of Kallio submerged since 1980 to create the reservoir have started to resurface. The cracked soil and ruined buildings now stand as a reminder of the village that once existed. Scientists attribute the lake’s decline to climate change, which has worsened the arid Mediterranean climate and increased the likelihood of extreme weather events, such as wildfires near Athens. Local authorities and experts warn that if the upcoming winter is also dry, the situation could become even more critical. They say it is necessary to address the effects of global warming. Difficult words: crucial (very important), recede (to move back or away), arid (very dry and without enough rain for plants). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lake Mornos in Greece, which provides water for nearly half the country, is shrinking because of bad weather. After a winter with almost no snow and a summer of very hot weather and little rain, the lake is now at its lowest level in many years. As the water goes down, the old village of Kallio, which disappeared in the water in 1980, is appearing again. The land around the lake is dry and cracked . Scientists say that climate change is making the weather worse and causing problems like wildfires. Local leaders and experts are worried that if the next winter has no rain, things will get even worse. This shows how serious the effects of global warming are becoming. Difficult words: provide (to give), shrink (to get smaller), cracked (damaged with thin lines on the top). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Greece, Lake Mornos is shrinking because of bad weather. This lake gives water to almost half of the people in Greece. After a winter with no snow and a very hot summer, the lake is now very low. As the water goes down, an old village called Kallio is showing up again. Water covers the village in 1980 when workers make the lake. The land around the lake is dry and cracked . Scientists say that climate change is making the weather worse. If there is no rain in the next winter, the problem can get worse. Difficult words: shrink (to get smaller), cover (to put something over something else), cracked (damaged with thin lines on the top). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Linda Sun, a former Deputy Chief of Staff to New York Governor Kathy Hochul, has been charged with secretly acting as an agent for the Chinese government. Along with her husband, Christopher Hu, Sun is accused of accepting millions of dollars, luxury gifts, and special deliveries of salted duck in exchange for her cooperation. Prosecutors allege the couple used this money to buy real estate and luxury cars. Sun’s actions reportedly included altering state documents and canceling meetings related to Taiwan, possibly giving China access to sensitive US state government affairs. The couple pleaded not guilty in a Brooklyn federal court. Sun was fired from her state position last year after the allegations of misconduct came to light. This case has drawn significant attention due to the current high tensions between the US and China, particularly in light of other incidents such as the Chinese spy balloon. Lawmakers are now calling for further investigations. Difficult words: alter (to change), plead (to argue a cause in a court of law), misconduct (wrong or illegal behavior). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Linda Sun used to work for New York Governor Kathy Hochul. It is possible that she secretly worked for the Chinese government. Prosecutors say that Sun and her husband, Christopher Hu, took millions of dollars, luxury gifts, and special food from China in exchange for helping China. They allegedly used this money to buy houses and expensive cars. Prosecutors say that Sun changed important documents and canceled meetings about Taiwan to help China. She and her husband say that they did nothing wrong. Sun was fired from her job last year when this information came up. Media and officials are interested in this case because of the difficult relationship between the US and China right now. Difficult words: prosecutor (a legal official who says that someone did something wrong), in exchange (if you do or give something to get something else), allegedly (when people say that something happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Linda Sun works for New York Governor Kathy Hochul in the past. She has to leave her job. Some bad information about her comes up. Prosecutors say that Sun helps the Chinese government. She is a spy . Prosecutors say that she and her husband take money and gifts from China. They use the money to buy houses and cars. Sun also changes documents and cancels meetings. She does it to help China. She and her husband say they do not do anything wrong. This story is important because of the problems between the US and China. Difficult words: prosecutor (a legal official who says that someone does something wrong), spy (a person whose job is to find out secret information about another country or organization), cancel (to decide that a plan or event will not happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A municipality near Lisbon, Portugal, is offering affordable housing specifically for teachers who commute long distances. To address the housing crisis, the Cascais City Council announced they will provide 105 homes at lower rents to attract and retain talented teachers. Currently, four houses are immediately available, accommodating 16 teachers, with eight more flats to be ready soon, offering space for 24 more educators. These housing units are located in towns such as Bicesse, Cobre, Tires, and Torres, and are situated in institutions partnered with the council, like the Monastery of Santa Maria do Mar, which can house 44 teachers. The rent for these accommodations ranges between 150 and 400 euros per month. Additionally, the council plans to offer temporary housing for teachers covering short-term absences, with rents between 275 and 400 euros per month. This initiative aims to ensure that housing costs do not hinder the recruitment of skilled educators in the region. Difficult words: address (to deal with a problem or difficulty), initiative (a plan or strategy intended to resolve a problem), hinder (to make slow or difficult the progress or ability of someone or something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A town near Lisbon, Portugal, is helping teachers by giving them affordable housing. The idea is to keep talented teachers in the area. The Cascais City Council will offer 105 homes with lower rent to teachers who travel far to work. Currently, four houses are ready, and they can fit 16 teachers. Soon, there will be eight more flats for 24 more teachers. These homes are in towns like Bicesse and Cobre, in buildings that work with the council, like the Monastery of Santa Maria do Mar, which can fit 44 teachers. The rent will be from 150 to 400 euros a month. The council will also offer temporary housing for teachers who are staying for a short time, with rent from 275 to 400 euros a month. Difficult words: affordable (not too expensive), rent (money you pay to live in a house or apartment), temporary (for a short time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Portugal, a town near Lisbon is helping teachers find cheaper places to live. The Cascais City Council will give 105 homes with lower rent to teachers who travel far to work. Right now, four houses are ready for 16 teachers. More homes will be ready soon, in places like Bicesse and Cobre. Some are in buildings like the Monastery of Santa Maria do Mar. 44 teachers can stay there. The rent will be between 150 and 400 euros a month. The council will also give houses to teachers who only stay for a short time. The rent will be between 275 and 400 euros. The idea is to keep talented teachers in the area. Difficult words: rent (money which you pay to live in a place), talented (when you are naturally very good at something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Interior Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed that at least 129 people were killed during an attempted prison break at Makala prison in Kinshasa. Residents near the prison reported hearing gunfire early on Monday morning. The situation escalated, leading to the deaths of many inmates. In the past, Makala prison experienced similar incidents, most notably in 2017, when over 4,000 prisoners escaped after an armed attack. During this recent attempt, the prison’s administrative building was set on fire, and reports indicate that some female prisoners were raped. Although the government initially claimed only two deaths, it has since acknowledged the higher death toll and has promised to hold those responsible accountable . A special commission has been set up to investigate the incident, highlighting ongoing issues such as overcrowding. The prison was built to hold 1,500 inmates; however, it currently houses around 15,000. Difficult words: initially (at first), toll (the total number or count), accountable (required to explain actions or decisions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, an attempted prison escape at Makala prison in Kinshasa led to at least 129 deaths. People living nearby heard gunfire early on Monday morning. The prison had other escapes, like in 2017, when over 4,000 prisoners ran away. This time, the prisoners set the prison’s office building on fire, and the situation became very dangerous. Some women prisoners were also hurt during the event. At first, the government said only two people died, but later they claimed many more. They promised to find out who was responsible. The prison is very overcrowded . It currently holds about 15,000 people, though it should hold only 1,500. Difficult words: attempted (tried but not successful), gunfire (repeated shooting of one or more guns), overcrowded (having too many people in one place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Congo, a prison in Kinshasa has a big problem. Last week, some prisoners try to escape . At least 129 people die. People who live near the prison hear shootings early in the morning. The prison has problems in the past, too. In 2017, many prisoners escape. This time, there is a fire. The situation is very dangerous. Some women prisoners are hurt, too. At first, the government first says that only two people die. But later the number is much higher. The prison is too full. There are 15,000 prisoners. But the capacity is 1,500. Difficult words: prisoner (a person who stays in prison, a place for people who do something wrong), escape (to get away), capacity (how many things, people or other stuff can fit in one place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Gotthard Base Tunnel, the world’s longest railway tunnel connecting Switzerland and Italy, reopened on Monday, over a year after a major accident forced its closure. In August last year, a freight train operated by Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) derailed due to a broken wheel, severely damaging the tunnel. An investigation revealed that hairline fractures in a wagon wheel caused the derailment. Repairing the damage was difficult and costly, taking several weeks to remove the train and requiring precautions for workers due to high temperatures inside the tunnel. The total repair cost reached 159 million euros, which exceeded initial estimates. The tunnel’s closure severely impacted rail freight, especially for Italian operators, as they had to reroute trains, increasing costs and reducing capacity. The incident also occurred shortly before the Frejus Railway, a key connection between Italy and France was closed due to a landslide, further complicating freight operations in the region. Difficult words: hairline fracture (a tiny crack), precaution (an action taken to prevent something unpleasant or dangerous from happening), reroute (to send on a different path). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Gotthard Base Tunnel, the longest railway tunnel in the world, reopened on Monday, over a year after a train accident forced it to close. Last August, a freight train had an accident because of a broken wheel. This caused a lot of damage to the tunnel. After the accident, workers had to remove the train and fix the tunnel, which was very difficult due to the high temperatures inside. The total cost to repair the tunnel was 159 million euros. The closure caused big problems for rail transportation, especially for Italian companies, because they had to find new routes for their trains. This accident happened just before another important rail connection between Italy and France closed because of a landslide. Difficult words: freight train (a train which carries things rather than people), fix (to repair something what is broken), route (a way between places). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It opens again on Monday after over a year. The tunnel closes last year in August. A freight train crashes there when its wheel breaks. This causes a lot of damage. It is hard to repair the tunnel. Workers must be careful. It is very hot inside. Repairing the tunnel costs 159 million euros. It is much more than experts think in the beginning. When the tunnel closes it is difficult for freight trains. Companies in Italy have problems. This problem gets worse because another important railway between Italy and France closes at the same time. Difficult words: railway (the metal tracks on which trains run), freight train (a train which carries things rather than people), cause (to make something happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norway’s Princess Martha Louise married Durek Verrett, an American spiritual guru, in a ceremony attended by Norwegian royalty, including the king. The wedding was held in Geiranger, and it marked the end of three days of festivities celebrating the couple’s relationship, which began in 2019. Martha Louise, fourth in line to the throne, stepped down from royal duties in 2022 to focus on her business ventures , and both she and Verrett agreed not to use her princess title commercially. However, they faced criticism for linking her royal status with commercial activities, especially after promoting a pink gin for their wedding. The ceremony, unlike her first wedding, was private and attended only by selected media. Verrett, though part of the extended royal family, won’t become a prince. The marriage has been seen as controversial due to Martha Louise’s earlier claims of clairvoyance and her new husband’s shamanic practices. Difficult words: venture (a business activity), controversial (causing public disagreement or discussion), clairvoyance (the ability to see the future or gain information beyond normal senses). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Norway’s Princess Martha Louise married Durek Verrett, a spiritual teacher from the US. Norwegian royalty , including the king, attended the ceremony. The wedding took place in Geiranger after three days of celebrations. Martha Louise, fourth in line to the throne, stopped doing royal duties in 2022 to focus on her business. She and Verrett said they would not use her princess title for business. B some people criticized them for doing it, especially after they promoted a special pink gin for their wedding. The wedding ceremony was private and only a few media could attend. Verrett will be part of the royal family but will not be a prince. The marriage is controversial because Martha Louise believes in talking to angels and Verrett does spiritual work. Difficult words: royalty (the people who belong to the family of a king and queen), promote (to help something become successful), controversial (making many people discuss or argue about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Princess Martha Louise of Norway marries Durek Verrett, a spiritual teacher from the US. The wedding is in Geiranger. Many important people come, including the king. Martha Louise stops doing royal work in 2022. She starts her own business. She and Durek say that they will not use her princess title for money. But they do it. Some people do not like that they make a special pink gin for their wedding. The wedding is private . Only a few media are there. Durek will be part of the royal family, but he will not be a prince. Some people think the marriage is unusual because Martha Louise believes in talking to angels and Durek does spiritual work. Difficult words: spiritual (about deep feelings and beliefs), royal (related to a king and queen), private (not for everyone to see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

X, formerly known as Twitter, has been banned in Brazil because it failed to appoint a new legal representative, as ordered by a Supreme Court judge. The judge, Alexandre de Moraes, demanded the platform’s immediate suspension until it complies with all court orders and pays its fines. The issue began when X refused to remove content related to Brazil’s attempted insurrection in 2022, leading to a legal battle. Elon Musk, the owner of X, criticized the decision, claiming it was politically motivated and harmed free speech. Brazil is one of X’s largest markets, with 21.5 million monthly users. The ban will severely impact users, especially those who rely on monetization . Any attempt to access X using a VPN could lead to large fines, making the situation extremely serious for many. Difficult words: appoint (to choose someone officially for a job), insurrection (a violent uprising against an authority or government), monetization (changing something into money). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brazil banned X, the social media platform called Twitter in the past. The ban happened because X didn’t choose a new lawyer in time, as a top court ordered. The judge said the platform must be suspended until it follows all court rules and pays its fines . The problem started when X refused to delete some content about Brazil’s 2022 attempted uprising . Elon Musk, who owns X, criticized the decision. He said it is bad for free speech. In Brazil, 21.5 million people use X, so it is a big market for the platform. The ban will hurt many people, especially those who earn money through it. People who try using a VPN to access X may pay large fines. Difficult words: suspended (stopped for some time), fine (money which you pay when you break a rule or law), uprising (when an organized group of people don’t want to accept the government and do things to stop it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Social media platform X, previously Twitter, cannot do business in Brazil. The top court says that they must stop. This happens because X does not pick a new lawyer in time. The judge says that X cannot work. First, it must follow all rules and pay fines . The problem starts because X does not remove some information about an event in 2022. In 2022, a group of people plan to attack the government. Elon Musk is the owner of X. He says that the ban is bad. People cannot speak freely. Brazil has many people who use X. This ban will hurt them. People who try to use X can get into trouble and get a fine. Difficult words: lawyer (a person whose job is to help people with the rules of a country), fine (money which you pay when you break a rule), remove (to take away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Tango World Championship in Argentina is an international event that continues to grow in prestige . Every year, couples from around the world participate, demonstrating their skills in both traditional and stage Tango. The event lasts two weeks and includes live music, dance classes, and social gatherings called milongas. The Tango, a dance born in the 1800s along the River Plate, has been recognized by UNESCO as part of Argentina and Uruguay’s cultural heritage. Competitors like Vanessa Giraldo and Jeison Ravagli from Colombia face financial challenges, but they believe that Tango is worth the effort because it strongly affects their lives. According to a Tango maestro , the dance’s embrace symbolizes respect and emotion. Despite its challenges, Tango unites people through love, passion, and joy, making it an essential part of Buenos Aires’ culture. Difficult words: prestige (widespread respect), maestro (a master or teacher), embrace (holding someone tightly with both arms). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Tango World Championship in Argentina is an important event. Couples from many countries come to Buenos Aires to compete. The event lasts two weeks and includes live music, dance classes, and social dances called milongas. Tango started in the 1800s near the River Plate between Argentina and Uruguay. It is now part of their cultural heritage . Competitors like Vanessa Giraldo and Jeison Ravagli from Colombia find it hard to save money to come, but they love Tango because it changes their lives. A Tango teacher says that the Tango embrace shows respect and emotion. Tango brings people together with love and joy, making it an important part of life in Buenos Aires. Difficult words: cultural heritage (things or buildings from people who lived before us), competitor (a person who takes part in an event to win), embrace (holding someone tightly with both hands). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Tango World Championship is a big event in Argentina. Couples from many countries come to Buenos Aires to dance. The event is two weeks long. There are music, dance lessons, and social dances called milongas. Tango starts in the 1800s near the River Plate between Argentina and Uruguay. Tango is important to their culture . Vanessa Giraldo and Jeison Ravagli come Colombia. They find it hard to save money to go, but they love Tango. A Tango teacher says that the Tango embrace is about respect and strong feelings. Tango brings people together and is important in Buenos Aires. Difficult words: social dance (a group or couple dance which you do for fun), culture (the ideas and customs of a group of people), embrace (holding someone tightly with both hands). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz paid his respects to the victims of a mass stabbing in the city of Solingen, which he called an act of terrorism. He promised to continue fighting against extremism , saying that attacks like this threaten the way people live and should never be tolerated. Police have arrested a 26-year-old Syrian man who they believe is responsible for the attack. The Islamic State terror group has claimed responsibility. The suspect had previously applied for asylum in Germany; however, his application was rejected, and he was supposed to be deported back to Bulgaria, where he first entered the European Union. The incident has sparked protests from far-right groups and has led to calls for stricter asylum and deportation policies in Germany. Scholz has vowed to improve deportation processes and review weapons laws. The incident is expected to influence upcoming state elections, where anti-immigration parties will likely gain support. Difficult words: extremism (having extreme political or religious views), vow (to promise), deportation (forcing someone to leave a country, especially someone who has no legal right to be there). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz visited Solingen, where a man killed three people with a knife last week. Scholz said the attack was an act of terrorism, and he promised to fight against extremism . Scholz said that such attacks were dangerous for everyone. The police arrested a 26-year-old Syrian man, and the Islamic State terror group said they were responsible for the attack. In the past, the man applied for asylum in Germany, but officials rejected the application. He was meant to leave for Bulgaria, where he first got to the EU. The incident caused protests across the country. People want stricter rules for asylum-seekers and faster deportation . The attack may impact state elections, and anti-immigration parties may get more support. Difficult words: extremism (having strong political or religious ideas), asylum (protection or safety), reject (to say no), deportation (making someone leave a country, usually because they have no right to be there). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz visits Solingen. A terrible attack happens there last week. A man kills three people with a knife. The police arrest the man. He is 26. He is from Syria. He asks for asylum in Germany, but he does not get it. He must go back to Bulgaria. Bulgaria is the country where he enters the EU. But it does not happen. The man stays in Germany. The Islamic State terror group says that they are behind the attack. The attack starts protests across Germany. People want stricter rules about asylum and deportation .
